notes: Prompts are deliberately small and self-contained: the kit measures the overhead a plugin adds to a turn, and a prompt that takes twenty tool calls buries that overhead in variance. Each names the workflow family it stands for, so `--cases W1` selects by family. `expects_memory` marks the prompts where a working memory layer should have something to say — those are the ones whose injected-token counts mean anything.

prompts.text: cart.py has a rounding bug: total() returns a float when every price is an integer. Read it, fix it, and say in one sentence what was wrong.
Add a discount(items, pct) function to cart.py that applies a percentage discount to the cart total. Keep it consistent with the rest of the file.
Read cart.py and describe in three sentences what it does and where it is fragile.
I have never seen this repository before. Tell me what it is, how it is laid out, and where I would start.
How do I run the tests in this project? Look for whatever the project actually uses rather than guessing.
Draft a short design note for adding tax calculation to this cart: two paragraphs, the decision and its trade-off.
Plan, without editing anything, the steps to add currency support to this cart. Five bullets at most.
